tone_statements.quote: Phonetic vowel length (mainly aa) does not seem frequent except, again, in T. sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp.22-24) covers consonants, vowels, prenasalization/palatalization/labialization; sec. 6.5.4 (p.30) compares Choogen Tsagu vs Choogen Dirya wordlists (final nasal); Appendix G p.64: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 348-item Choogen wordlists are tone-marked, no stress marks. Sec. 3 states the only prior linguistic data on Choogen are Skinner 1977 and Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994.

tone.quote: The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features. Some vowels are transcribed with the IPA symbol for vowel lengthening [ː] others are represented as geminate vowels.
tone.locator: p. 65, Appendix G: Wordlists, introductory note, second paragraph (S's 'p. 64' is off by one: p. 1); Choogen / Choogen D wordlist rows run pp. 65-111
tone.says: No tonal analysis (p. 65: 'no in-depth analysis of tones'), but the 348-item Choogen (village Tsagu, Ganjuwa LGA, speaker IS, J. Dabet 2020/8/19) and Choogen D (= 'Dirya Choogen' of Laya) wordlists in Appendix G are transcribed with impressionistic three-level pitch diacritics (grave/macron/acute, e.g. vìnànɛ̄, pìrāmɛ̄, àtúkɛ̄, āːtītsī); number of contrastive tones not stated.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena. (T = Tsagu/Civogai, informant Dano Sheka)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' p.5: o/e and phonetic vowel length (mainly aa) more frequent in T (Tsagu) than in the other languages; 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' Comparative wordlist only.

tone.quote: Phonetic vowel length (mainly aa) does not seem frequent except, again, in T. As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.
tone.locator: p. 5 (AAL 4:5), section 2 'The phonetic inventory', end of the vowel paragraph
tone.n_tones: 3 levels + falling heard (phonetic, group-wide; not analysed)
tone.says: Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory', p. 5: for the North Bauchi recordings as a group (Tsagu = T included, and T singled out in the same paragraph for o/e and vowel length) Skinner heard 'usually three levels and a falling' and confirmed tonal minimal pairs of monosyllables, but left all forms untoned as too impressionistic. Group-wide phonetic remark, not a Tsagu-specific toneme analysis.
